text: {"resumen":"A Kerberos service ticket (event 4769, rule 100212) was requested for the honeytoken service account svc_sql_backup by account crojas@LAB.LOCAL from 192.168.56.103 (Kali, the simulated attacker host), with RC4 encryption (0x17) and Failure Code 0x0, so the ticket was issued. This is consistent with Kerberoasting.","razonamiento":"Per the trusted context, svc_sql_backup exists only as a tripwire, so any ticket request for it is high priority and near-zero false positive. The request came from 192.168.56.103 (Kali), the known attacker host, with RC4 (0x17) and the ticket was issued (Failure Code 0x0). The account crojas@LAB.LOCAL may be compromised or misused, so a human should review before any disruptive action. I suggest escalation to tier 2 rather than automatic disabling.","prioridad":"high","confianza":"high","mitre_id":"T1558.003","campos_sustento":["rule_id","event_id","mitre_id","service_name","src_ip","target_user","raw_log","description","dest_ip"],"accion_sugerida":"escalate_tier2","verificaciones_sugeridas":["Confirm how crojas@LAB.LOCAL's credentials ended up being used from 192.168.56.103 (Kali): look for prior 4624/4625 events and any Kerberos TGT requests (4768) for that account from that source.","Look for other 4769 requests from 192.168.56.103 in the same period, especially RC4 tickets for other SPNs (rule 100211), to gauge the extent of the activity.","Verify with the owner of crojas whether the activity was expected, and whether the account should be reset if it is not.","Check whether the svc_sql_backup ticket was later used for logons or access to services, and review the strength and last change of that account's password.","Check for follow-on activity (successful logons with svc_sql_backup, lateral movement) from 192.168.56.103 or hosts reached from it."],"possible_prompt_injection":false}

{"resumen":"Rule 100230 (event 4662, Read Property) fired for an audited read by the Administrator account of an AD user object. The pipeline field decoy_verified is true, so the object GUID matches the decoy account adm_backup_legacy. The alert has no src_ip, so the originating host is unknown.","razonamiento":"decoy_verified = true means an account that no person or service uses was read, which is high priority. Account discovery (T1087.002) is only a hypothesis, because a single read can also come from a broad directory query by an admin tool or script. Since the subject is the built-in Administrator (SID ending in -500) and the source host is missing, the action is escalation for human review rather than a disruptive step.","prioridad":"high","confianza":"medium","mitre_id":"T1087.002","campos_sustento":["rule_id","event_id","decoy_verified","subject_user","object_name","raw_log","dest_ip","mitre_id"],"accion_sugerida":"escalate_tier2","verificaciones_sugeridas":["Use Logon ID 0x5D6BE to find the matching 4624 logon event on DC01 and identify the source host/IP and logon type, since src_ip is null in this alert.","Look for other 4662 reads or LDAP queries from the same subject, Logon ID, or host around 2026-11-19T05:46:54.949+0000 that would indicate enumeration of many users rather than a single read.","Check whether an admin tool, inventory script, or scheduled directory query that lists all users ran at that time and could explain the read.","Confirm with the Administrator account owner whether this activity was theirs, and review recent logons and other activity of this account for signs of credential misuse.","Check for follow-on activity involving adm_backup_legacy, such as logon attempts or Kerberos ticket requests."],"possible_prompt_injection":false}

{"resumen":"Rule 100230 (event 4662, Read Property) fired on DC01 (192.168.56.10): the account Administrator read an audited user-class object. The SOC pipeline set decoy_verified to true, so the object GUID matches the decoy account adm_backup_legacy. No source IP is present in the alert.","razonamiento":"decoy_verified is true, so an account that no person or service uses was read, which warrants high priority. The subject is the built-in Administrator (SID ending in -500), a privileged account. Account discovery (T1087.002) is only a hypothesis, because a single read can also come from a broad directory query by an admin tool or inventory script. With no src_ip and no other enumeration visible, confidence is medium and a human should review before any action; disabling the account is not warranted on this evidence.","prioridad":"high","confianza":"medium","mitre_id":"T1087.002","campos_sustento":["rule_id","event_id","decoy_verified","subject_user","object_name","dest_ip","raw_log","mitre_id"],"accion_sugerida":"escalate_tier2","verificaciones_sugeridas":["Identify the origin of Logon ID 0x5D6BE: find the matching 4624 logon event on DC01 and its source IP and logon type, since the alert has no src_ip.","Check whether the same subject or host read many other user objects around 2026-11-19T05:46:54.981+0000 (a broad directory query or enumeration pattern, such as a burst of 4662 events), which would corroborate account discovery.","Ask the Administrator account owner whether an admin tool, inventory script or AD audit ran at that time.","Check for other activity from the same Logon ID or host, such as LDAP queries, new group memberships, Kerberos ticket requests or failed logons.","Confirm the object GUID against the decoy's objectGUID again and check whether the decoy was accessed at other times."],"possible_prompt_injection":false}

{"resumen":"Event 4728 (rule 100220, level 13) shows the Administrator account added the member CN=Carlos Rojas,OU=TI,DC=lab,DC=local to the Domain Admins group (RID 512) on the domain controller 192.168.56.10. No source IP is present and there is no evidence in the alert that the change was approved.","razonamiento":"A member added to Domain Admins is one of the highest-signal AD events and must be treated as critical unless approval is shown by trusted context, which is absent here. The actor is the built-in Administrator account (SID ending in -500), which may be legitimate admin work or a compromised credential; the alert alone cannot distinguish them, so escalation for human verification is preferred over a disruptive action.","prioridad":"critical","confianza":"medium","mitre_id":"T1098","campos_sustento":["rule_id","event_id","description","dest_ip","target_user","subject_user","raw_log","mitre_id"],"accion_sugerida":"escalate_tier2","verificaciones_sugeridas":["Confirm with the IT/AD owners whether adding Carlos Rojas to Domain Admins was an approved change, using a ticket or channel independent of the alert","Review the Administrator logon session (Logon ID 0x119230): the originating host, logon type and the 4624 event that created it","Check for other activity by Administrator around the same time, such as other group changes, new accounts, or password resets","Inspect Carlos Rojas's account: creation date, recent logons, and any activity since the group change","Verify the current membership of Domain Admins against the expected baseline","If the change is not approved, plan removal from the group and credential resets for the involved accounts, with human approval"],"possible_prompt_injection":false}
